aggressive_definition_excerpt: Furthermore, 16:1n-7 levels were positively related to incidence of high-grade (Gleason score ≥7) tumors
study_design: Matched case-control analysis within the Physicians' Health Study using prediagnostic blood samples from incident cases and an equal number of controls.
reason: The study reports both overall incident prostate cancer and incident high-grade prostate cancer. Although 476 cases and an equal number of controls are stated, the total analytic sample is not explicitly reported and therefore is not inferred. The abstract does not explicitly establish the underlying analysis as a prospective cohort or nested case-control design.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Blood levels of 16:1n-7 were associated with higher prostate cancer incidence, with rate ratios for men in increasing quintiles of 1.00, 1.40, 1.35, 1.44, and 1.97 (95% confidence interval: 1.27-3.06; Ptrend = 0.003).
estimate_classifications.reason: The supplied 1.97 estimate is for overall prostate cancer incidence, not specifically high-grade disease.

additional_estimates.comparison: Highest versus lowest quintile of blood 16:1n-7 levels
additional_estimates.effect_excerpt: Furthermore, 16:1n-7 levels were positively related to incidence of high-grade (Gleason score ≥7) tumors (rate ratioQ5-Q1 = 3.92; 95% confidence interval: 1.72-8.94) but not low-grade tumors (rate ratioQ5-Q1 = 1.51; 95% confidence interval: 0.87-2.62) (Pheterogeneity = 0.02).
